hints.title: Manhattan Distance Definition
hints.text: The distance between cell (r, c) and center (rCenter, cCenter) is abs(r - rCenter) + abs(c - cCenter). All cells must be ordered from smallest to largest distance.

hints.title: Coordinate Generation
hints.text: Iterate through all r in [0, rows - 1] and c in [0, cols - 1] to enumerate all valid matrix coordinates.

hints.title: Sort or BFS Traversal
hints.text: Sort the coordinates directly using their Manhattan distance as the key, or explore outwards level by level starting from the center.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def allCellsDistOrder(self, rows: int, cols: int, rCenter: int, cCenter: int) -> list[list[int]]:
        cells = [[r, c] for r in range(rows) for c in range(cols)]
        cells.sort(key=lambda p: abs(p[0] - rCenter) + abs(p[1] - cCenter))
        return cells
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recomputing distances in an unindexed fashion without sorting fails to satisfy order requirements.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting all R * C cells takes near-linear time and produces the exact sorted coordinate array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should enumerate coordinates and sort by Manhattan distance or use bucket sort / BFS.
complexity.notes: Can also be achieved in linear O(R * C) time using BFS or bucket sort on distances up to R + C.
